payload.root_cause: In slugify (src/text.js:11), the whitespace/dash collapsing replace uses the regex /[\s-]+/ WITHOUT the global flag `g`. String.prototype.replace with a non-global regex only substitutes the FIRST match, so only the first gap between words is converted to a dash; every later run of spaces/dashes is left as-is. For 'Hello Big  World!' this yields 'hello-big  world' (the double space before 'world' survives) instead of the expected 'hello-big-world'. The other replaces in the chain (lines 10 and 12) correctly use `g`, making line 11 the inconsistent, buggy one.

payload.rationale: The root cause is that the second `.replace` in `slugify` uses the regex `/[\s-]+/` without the `g` flag. In JavaScript, `String.prototype.replace` with a non-global regex only substitutes the FIRST match, so only the first run of whitespace/dashes becomes a dash and all later gaps survive. Adding the `g` flag makes the replace substitute every run of whitespace/dashes, consistent with the `g`-flagged regexes on the lines before and after it. Hand-tracing the tests confirms this: 'Hello Big  World!' → lowercase/trim → 'hello big  world!' → strip '!' → 'hello big  world' → with `g`, both the single space and the double space become '-' → 'hello-big-world' (no edge dashes to trim). Similarly '  Already-slugged  title ' → 'already-slugged  title' → with `g` the hyphen and double space both collapse to single dashes → 'already-slugged-title'. This is the smallest possible change (one added flag) and touches only the buggy line.
